name: Turkey
note: Turkey in the style of the Russian model tree: democratic government as the historical path and alternatives led by real parties of the data (left, conservative, nationalist, religious) plus a junta; economy (the programme after the 2001 crisis, the new lira, Marmaray, TurkStream), state and constitution (EU reforms, the 2010 and 2017 referendums, the 2016 coup attempt, the 2023 earthquakes), defence industry and drones, foreign policy. Sourced starting spirits in data/spirits/tur.json. Alternatives are a counterfactual.

source.title: Wikipedia: Accession of Turkey to the European Union

focuses.name: The direction of the country
focuses.description: Which camp governs the country.

focuses.name: Democratic government
focuses.description: Parties alternate in power through elections, as they historically did.

focuses.name: A turn to the left
focuses.description: Parties of the left (the DSP and the CHP) gain on wages, welfare and public services.

focuses.name: Unions and voters
focuses.description: Unions and young voters rally to the left.

focuses.name: A left-wing government
focuses.description: The most popular party of the democratic left leads the government.

focuses.name: Expand the welfare state
focuses.description: Public health care and higher pensions.

focuses.name: A conservative turn
focuses.description: Conservative parties (ANAP, the DYP and later the İYİ Party) gain on order, tax cuts and tradition.

focuses.name: Business and the countryside
focuses.description: Business and rural voters rally to the right.

focuses.name: A conservative government
focuses.description: The most popular conservative party leads the government.

focuses.name: Fiscal discipline
focuses.description: Cut spending and taxes to balance the budget.

focuses.name: A populist wave
focuses.description: National-populist parties (the MHP) gain on immigration and sovereignty.

focuses.name: Rallies and referendums
focuses.description: Mass rallies and calls for referendums.

focuses.name: A national-populist government
focuses.description: The most popular national-populist party leads the government.

focuses.name: Sovereignty first
focuses.description: Restrict immigration and limit the power of international bodies.

focuses.name: A religious turn
focuses.description: Religious parties (the Virtue Party, later the AKP and the Felicity Party) gain as faith returns to politics.

focuses.name: Faith networks
focuses.description: Congregations and charities organise.

focuses.name: A religious government
focuses.description: The most popular religious party leads the government.

focuses.name: Faith in public life
focuses.description: Religious education and an official religion.

focuses.name: The army steps in
focuses.description: With the state in crisis, the generals prepare to take over.

focuses.name: Military council
focuses.description: The armed forces remove the government. The coup may fail.

focuses.name: Martial order
focuses.description: A state of emergency, a curfew and military courts.

focuses.name: Return to the barracks
focuses.description: The council hands power to an elected government.

focuses.name: An economic programme
focuses.description: A stabilisation programme with the IMF after the crisis of February 2001.

focuses.name: Restructure the banks
focuses.description: Close failed banks and set up an independent bank regulator.

focuses.name: An independent central bank
focuses.description: Let the central bank target inflation.

focuses.name: The new Turkish lira
focuses.description: Replace the old lira with a new lira, as Turkey did in 2005.

focuses.name: Privatisation
focuses.description: Sell telecoms, refineries and state banks.

focuses.name: Anatolian tigers
focuses.description: Support the export industries of the Anatolian cities.

focuses.name: Construction boom
focuses.description: Housing, airports and bridges.

focuses.name: An energy hub
focuses.description: Pipelines across Turkey from the Caspian and Russia to Europe.

focuses.name: Marmaray
focuses.description: A rail tunnel under the Bosporus, opened on 29 October 2013.

focuses.name: TurkStream
focuses.description: A gas pipeline from Russia under the Black Sea, announced on 1 December 2014.

focuses.name: A nuclear power plant
focuses.description: Turkey's first nuclear plant on the Mediterranean.

focuses.name: Black Sea gas
focuses.description: Develop the gas found in the Black Sea.

focuses.name: State and constitution
focuses.description: Reform of the state and its constitution.

focuses.name: EU harmonisation packages
focuses.description: Laws that bring Turkey's rules into line with the European Union.

focuses.name: Accession negotiations
focuses.description: Membership negotiations with the European Union, opened on 3 October 2005.

focuses.name: The 2010 constitutional referendum
focuses.description: Amendments approved on 12 September 2010 with 58 percent.

focuses.name: A peace process
focuses.description: Talks with the PKK and reforms for Kurdish citizens.

focuses.name: After the coup attempt
focuses.description: Purge the coup plotters after the failed attempt of 15 July 2016.

focuses.name: An executive presidency
focuses.description: Amendments approved on 16 April 2017 abolish the post of prime minister.

focuses.name: After the earthquakes
focuses.description: Rebuild the south-east after the earthquakes of 6 February 2023. Unlocks rebuilding homes.

focuses.name: Health transformation
focuses.description: Universal health insurance and new hospitals. Unlocks city hospitals.

focuses.name: Schools and universities

focuses.name: Commando brigades

focuses.name: A national fighter

focuses.name: Cross-border operations
